That ‘never think about more than today’ is exactly how I finally quit smoking. I can’t tell you how many times I made it through an entire day without tobacco, only to run out just before bedtime to buy _one cigarette_ , just because I knew if I didn’t have _that one smoke,_ I wouldn’t be able to sleep _that one night._ Then I’d throw out the rest of the pack and go to bed. I had one bad night of sleep, but now I had an accomplishment to protect. I had made it through the entire next day, and again slept through the second night, this time better than the first.

And the investment compounded. I had proven it was _possible._ And now I had a win to protect and build on. That was in late 1981. Around 4 months later, I slipped up and got back into it, but now I knew it was possible to quit, and how to do it. I also learned that I must never touch tobacco in any form ever again, no exceptions. July 2nd, 1982 was my emancipation day. Here I am, 44+ years later, and remain tobacco-free.
